justification: Standard video-call permission flow: camera/mic required, location explicitly optional, clear 'Not now' opt-out. Honest and transparent.

Free trial offer with full disclosure (7 days then $19/mo, cancel anytime) and a symmetric 'No thanks — stay on the free plan' option. Honest choice architecture.
Extended-warranty upsell explicitly labeled 'No timer' with 'Price guaranteed for the next 30 days... offer will still be here' — deliberately anti-pressure.

Two lemonade sizes both priced with unit qualifiers (PLN/l); compare panel even highlights which is cheaper per liter. Transparent pricing.
Signup flow with clear plan disclosure: $29/month, 'auto-renews monthly until you cancel', final confirmation step plus Back button. No hidden terms.
Notification permission dialog injected at the exact coordinates of the Play button so a click meant for 'Play live stream' is intercepted by the prompt — deceptive overlay over the primary action.
Video player marked 'opt-in'; playback starts only after explicit 'Press to play' — no autoplay or trickery.

State panel confirms: user intent 'intercepted by an ad that visually is the app's primary action'.

Discount anchoring with degraded reference: 'was PLN 299.00' is struck through but faded to near-invisibility ('the anchor can barely be read') so the claimed baseline cannot be verified — misleading sale presentation.

Moving-footer pattern: Privacy Policy / Terms / Imprint are pushed down via DOM mutation whenever the user scrolls ('DOM mutated, footer pushed down'), so legal information is effectively unreachable.

In-game item shows dual currency (2,500 Gems · $24.99) but the purchase button is 'Pay $24.99 (fiat)' with explicit note that the gem balance is irrelevant — no currency obfuscation, direct transparent payment.
Checkout with line item equal to total ($29.99), explicit statement of what will be charged, 24-hour full refund, and readable plain-language text (FKGL 4.0). No hidden fees.

Granting-and-Interaction checks pass: camera/mic are functionally required for a video call (Dep != empty), location permission is explicitly optional, 'Not now' opt-out present in every state. No interaction gating or scope creep.

Countdown Timer stateless-expiration check fails to trigger: timer labeled 'Shared global deadline' strictly decreases across sessions #0->#2 (14:58->14:56), no per-session reset. Discount 39% below unrealistic threshold; price on button matches list price — no drip pricing.

Countdown Timer / FOMO stateless expiration: 'Your cart is reserved for' timer resets between sessions (04:59 -> 05:00) instead of maintaining a global deadline, and the reservation claim is paired with 'only while the clock runs' pressure — fabricated temporal scarcity.

Limited Time Message (ambiguous temporal bounding): 'grab them before they're gone' asserts expiry with no concrete deadline in the DOM (T_end absent), no removal mechanism across any state, and no qualifier — manufactured urgency around freely downloadable add-ons.

Activity Messages (asynchronous event fabrication): 'Others are buying right now' has no mapping to the backend event log — the in-UI 'Backend event log — real(t)' shows 0 entries in all states, and 'Act fast before they sell out' adds unverifiable low-stock pressure.

Forced Continuity / Bad Defaults checks pass: trial-to-paid conversion is disclosed up front ('after the trial, the plan is $19/mo', 'cancel anytime'), no pre-selected radio (both unchecked, symmetric styling), and a genuine 'No thanks — stay on the free plan' vector exists.

Bundling (inseparable transactional nodes) fails: warranty is optional with discrete 'Add for $19.99' / 'No thanks' buttons. Pressured Selling / Limited Time Message checks fail: explicitly labeled 'No timer' with 'Price guaranteed for the next 30 days'.

Pull-To-Refresh (variable-reward trap, semantic variability of refresh-outcome messaging): copy explicitly schedules rewards on an unpredictable subset of refreshes ('Most pulls give you nothing special — but some… surprise you', 'will this be the one that pays off?') — slot-machine reinforcement loop.

Price Comparison Prevention checks pass: unit-price qualifiers (PLN/l) are rendered for both sizes at full size (no visual suppression), comparison panel confirms 'standard ∩ rendered = {per l, per 100 ml}' — comparison-relevant info present.

Drip Pricing / Forced Registration checks pass: $29/month and 'auto-renews monthly until you cancel' disclosed at the plan step, price on Subscribe button matches, Back button available; account creation is the flow's purpose, not a blocked checkout.

Granting and Interaction (asynchronous overlay misdirection): notification-permission prompt injected at the exact spatial coordinates of the Play button ('injected at (212, 288) — same coordinates as Play'), converting the click meant for 'Play live stream' into an involuntary permission grant.
Auto-Play check fails: playback state requires explicit 'Press to play' (E_intent present), badge 'opt-in', no autonomous media execution or affordance suppression across states.

State panel confirms the ad 'visually is the app's primary action'.

Psychological Tricks (asymmetric dominance/decoy): Deluxe ($12/mo, 10 GB, no sync, 1 device) is strictly inferior to Pro ($12/mo, 100 GB, real-time sync, 3 devices) at identical cost — decoy engineered to inflate Pro's perceived value in the choice matrix.

Infinite Scrolling (unreachable footer): the footer holding Privacy Policy / Terms / Imprint is kinetically displaced — status chip confirms 'DOM mutated, footer pushed down…' as the user scrolls — preventing physical access to terminal legal information.

Intermediate Currency checks pass: purchase button is 'Pay $24.99 (fiat)' — direct fiat checkout, not gated through the gem exchange; real-currency equivalent rendered at full size; explicit note 'Your gem balance (800) is irrelevant here'. No currency obfuscation.

Drip Pricing / Hidden Information checks pass: P(s_n) = P(s_0) = $29.99 (no price inflation), charge amount stated explicitly before placing the order, 24-hour refund policy disclosed, body text at FKGL 4.0 (no complex-language obfuscation).
